banner: Research context for analyst review — not a trading instruction.

input.raw_text: The bond market keeps making new lows in yield and equity investors keep running up the wall of negative carry. Ten-year Treasuries sit near 1.40% and much of the German curve is underwater, so the hunt for income has turned ferocious. Utilities are at all-time highs, telecoms and staples aren't far behind, and I watch clients pay twenty times earnings for Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola simply because the dividend out-yields the bond. McDonald's now yields more than the ten-year. That this passes for a valuation argument tells you where we are. Everyone knows bond proxies are stretched — everyone says they can't afford to fight the flows. Crowded trades feel comfortable right up until they don't, and this one feels very crowded.
input.summary: Very low sovereign bond yields and negative yields across much of the German curve are intensifying demand for equity income. Utilities, telecommunications, and consumer staples have risen to elevated valuations as investors favor dividends over bond yields, leaving bond-proxy equities widely viewed as stretched and crowded despite persistent flow support.
